result.title: Efficient Learning of Survival Analysis Models Under Outcome-Dependent Truncation and Censoring
result.summary: Modern machine learning models are typically trained on data assumed to be representative of the predictive tasks the model will face in the future, but practical datasets violate this assumption. We focus on outcome-dependent truncation in which an observation appears in the training data depending on its label. Our work connects two largely distinct literatures: efficient learning under truncation and survival analysis. Existing methods for truncated survival analysis do not characterize the optimization landscape and instead rely on iterative procedures such as expectation maximization. We address this gap and prove that Cox regression can be efficiently learned under truncated and right-censored data using first-order optimization when the baseline hazard is known (despite nonconvexity). In contrast, when the baseline hazard is learned jointly, we construct identifiable and correctly specified models whose negative log-likelihood contains strict suboptimal local minima. On experiments with four survival datasets, we show that accounting for truncation reduces the prediction bias induced by naive Cox regression and extends to neural networks. We also show orders of magnitude speedups compared to standard expectation maximization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究结局依赖截断与右删失下的生存分析学习：证明基线风险已知时 Cox 回归可用一阶优化高效求解（尽管非凸），而在联合学习基线风险时构造出含严格次优局部极小值的可识别模型，并在四个数据集上验证考虑截断可降低预测偏差、相对 EM 显著加速。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「样本是否进入训练集取决于结局标签」的截断设定，可能类比 latent 推理中按答案正确性筛选轨迹带来的选择偏差；对非凸景观与次优局部极小值的刻画，可供核查轨迹训练与监督是否被数据筛选扭曲。
